turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Mr. Hale. Thank you for seeing me.

I have twenty minutes. Then a client call.

I'm here about Owen's Hamlet essay. You entered a zero before you called me.

Walk me through that. What did you see, and when?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for agreeing to meet in person.

Of course. But you haven't answered me.

The zero is already in the gradebook. Fifteen percent of his mark.

What date did you run the essay through the checker? Which tool? And what exactly did it show you?

I'd like to see the report. Not a summary. The report itself.
I'll admit I looked you up. Your firm's appellate record is remarkable.

That's not why I'm here.

My record has nothing to do with Owen's essay.

You looked me up. Fine. But you didn't look up the evidence first. You entered the zero first.

So again. What date did you run it? Which tool? And where is the report?
Someone with your training will appreciate that I'm simply following the evidence. I expect you'd do the same in my position.

Then show me the evidence.

A score isn't evidence. It's a number from a tool.

What's the tool's name? What's its documented error rate? Who validated it?

Did you look at his drafts? Version history? Anything he handed in before this one?

And did you speak to Owen before you entered the zero? Yes or no.
